description: The image displays four pie charts comparing the distribution of error types across four different language models — GPT4-o, Gemini1.5-Pro, Llama3.1-70B-Instruct, and Llama3.1-405B-Instruct — as evaluated by the FactBench benchmark for factual accuracy. Each chart is segmented by error category with labeled percentages and counts. For GPT4-o, “Lack of Knowledge” dominates at 83.3% (5 instances), with “Safety” accounting for 16.7% (1 instance). Gemini1.5-Pro shows a more diverse distribution: “Misinformation” at 38.4% (33), “Lack of Knowledge” at 22.1% (19), “Ethical Advice” at 16.3% (14), “Clarification” at 14.0% (12), and “Safety” at 9.3% (8). Llama3.1-70B-Instruct is split between “Lack of Knowledge” (75.0%, 3) and “Clarification” (25.0%, 1). Llama3.1-405B-Instruct shows an even split: “Lack of Knowledge” and “Misinformation” each at 50.0% (2 instances each). The charts use distinct colors for each category and include both percentage and absolute count labels within each slice, allowing for direct comparison of error prevalence across models.
